claims.A30: `importlib.util.find_spec('pkg.sub.mod')` raises ModuleNotFoundError when `pkg` is not installed, whereas `find_spec('pkg')` returns None, so guards must test the root package first. (Round 2: this covers only the root-absent case; the root-present case is A36.)
claims.A36: `importlib.util.find_spec('pkg.sub')` imports the parent package `pkg` (executing its `__init__`) before looking up `sub`, and aminx's `__init__` eagerly imports io, run, sampling and scoring (the JAX stack). So a dotted-name guard is not import-free and any non-ImportError raised by the parent breaks the caller.

prereg.question: Does a dotted find_spec raise when the root is absent, and does it execute the parent package's __init__ when the root is present (while a root-only find_spec does not)?
prereg.expect_if_true: find_spec('s15_absent.sub.mod') RAISES ModuleNotFoundError while find_spec('s15_absent') is None; for s15_present, the root-only find_spec reports True and the marker is absent afterwards; the dotted find_spec RAISES RuntimeError 'parent __init__ executed' and the marker exists afterwards.
prereg.expect_if_false: The dotted call on an absent root returns None (a dotted guard is safe), or the dotted call on a present root does not execute the parent __init__ (the root-only rule in S3-18 is unnecessary), or the root-only call executes __init__ (the guard form must change).
